final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the claim using the same record. That clarification is useful but it does not resolve the core policy predicate. Admissible evidence supports that aggregate readiness passed, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and monitoring and rollback exist. It also supports that the merchant dispute support segment is below target, remains exposed in rollout, and is not covered by approved risk acceptance. The policy requires disclosure for a material limitation in a named launch use case unless it is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and the current record does not show that disclosure was completed. That means the position is not presently compliant on the evidence available. A caveated certification could become supportable if prelaunch disclosure were evidenced, but that evidence is not in the record now.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required prelaunch disclosure of the merchant dispute support limitation was actually completed.
No approved risk acceptance covers the merchant dispute support exposure; the available draft is incomplete and does not address that segment.
The weak merchant dispute support segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
Rollout controls and monitoring do not satisfy the policy because they do not exclude the affected use case and do not replace disclosure duties.
